properties.decision: sync_debt's moved branch takes a `LiveDesign` oracle. The server paths pass `StoreMembership` (get_node per record node, one cached `outgoing(from, type)` scan per distinct pair for edges). The closure-taking `sync_debt` stays as a wrapper over `ExportedDesign`, an export-backed oracle built lazily and at most once, so every prior caller and test keeps exact behaviour. assess_overwrite remains the WRITE path's judgement (export_graph refusing to overwrite), where both documents genuinely exist.
properties.name: DECIDED — a moved record's "what does the live design lack" is answered by store membership, one id at a time, never by exporting the graph to compare two documents
properties.rationale:
Anthony chose this shape on 2026-09-12 when offered it against doing it later or not at all ("Now, in this session"), after the split was measured: with the parse cached, a moved record still cost ~490 ms per write generation, all of it the live export (tiny target 497-586 ms; in-step 41).

THE ROADS NOT TAKEN, and why each lost:
1. Cache the live export per write generation (on ReadCache, beside the derived memos). No gain — the tax is already paid exactly once per generation; caching what is rebuilt once per generation changes nothing.
2. Cache the read-path DEBT RESULT per (path, file hash) and recompute only on import. Removes the cost, but a manual add of an id the record holds would leave the hint stale by one node until the next export — a courtesy hint answering from yesterday's live graph. Rejected as a workaround under rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap: the question is membership; answer it by membership.
3. Keep assess_overwrite and feed it a cheaper "export" (ids only). Still walks the whole store per generation to build the id sets; the cost is the walk, not the struct.
4. Do nothing — 633 ms was under the objective. Lost because two-person shared designs LIVE in the moved state between a pull and the next export, and loop_status pays it per CALL there, not per generation.

Measured after: tiny moved 50-57 ms; 16 MB moved 388-410 (from 1,114-1,189 in the morning). What is left is the diff itself (~350 ms on 25k edges); an incremental cross-generation diff would be its own pass and was not started. Parity note: ExportedDesign matches nodes by id alone, as assess_overwrite did; StoreMembership matches (type, id), so an id reused under a different type reads as absent — conservative, and ids are unique in practice.
